note: Family recipes for /meal-prep/. Edit scripts/meals/src/recipes_*.py and run build_recipes.py; allergens, diet and guides are derived from the catalog.

recipes.name: Classic Cheeseburgers
recipes.summary: Juicy, simply seasoned burgers that cook on the grill or in a skillet in about 12 minutes.
steps: Divide the beef into 4 equal portions and shape each into a patty about 3/4 inch thick and a little wider than the buns. Press a shallow dimple into the center of each so it stays flat as it cooks. Handle the meat gently.
Wash your hands after shaping. Season both sides of the patties with the salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Heat the grill or a heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the patties 4 to 5 minutes per side, flipping once, until an instant-read thermometer in the center reads 160°F.
Lay a slice of cheese on each patty for the last minute; cover so it melts.
Toast the buns cut side down for 30 to 60 seconds. Move the cooked burgers to a clean plate, not the one that held the raw patties.
Build the burgers with lettuce, tomato and your choice of toppings.
recipes.make_ahead: Shape the patties up to 1 day ahead. Stack them with wax paper between and keep covered in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze raw patties with wax paper between them for 3 to 4 months for best quality. Thaw overnight in the fridge, or cook from frozen and add a few minutes per side.

leftovers.text: Chop a leftover patty into a quesadilla or over a salad; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Make a few small slider patties (about 2 ounces each) for little hands. They cook in about 3 minutes per side, still to 160°F.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free buns or wrap the burgers in lettuce leaves.
swaps.dairy_free: Leave off the cheese.
swaps.meatless: Cook store-bought veggie patties by the package directions and use the same toppings.

prep_day.ahead: Shape and season the patties; slice the tomato and onion.

recipes.name: Ground Beef Tacos
recipes.summary: Taco night with a homemade seasoning mix, so you know exactly what is in it.
steps: Cook the beef and onion in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and the beef reaches 160°F, about 7 minutes. Spoon off extra fat if there is a lot.
Stir in the chili powder, cumin, paprika, garlic powder, oregano, salt and pepper and cook 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the tomato sauce and water. Simmer 4 to 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick enough to hold on a spoon.
Warm the tortillas: wrap in a damp paper towel and microwave 30 to 45 seconds, or heat one at a time in a dry skillet.
Set out the filling and toppings so everyone can build their own.
recipes.make_ahead: Cook the filling up to 3 days ahead and keep it in the fridge. Reheat to 165°F, adding a splash of water.

freezer.text: Freeze the cooked filling flat in a freezer bag for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge overnight.

leftovers.text: Use leftover filling for taco salad, nachos or quesadillas the next day.

recipes.kids: Set up a build-your-own bar. Younger children often like the meat, cheese and tortilla separate on the plate.

swaps.gluten_free: Corn tortillas and this homemade seasoning are naturally free of wheat; check labels on the tortillas.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the cheese and sour cream; add extra avocado.
swaps.meatless: Use 2 cans of black or pinto beans, drained and lightly mashed, in place of the beef. Skip the browning step.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the taco filling; shred the lettuce and dice the tomato.

recipes.name: Classic Meat Lasagna
recipes.summary: Layers of meat sauce, ricotta and mozzarella. Make it on the weekend; it reheats beautifully.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the noodles 2 minutes less than the package says. Drain and lay them flat on an oiled baking sheet so they do not stick.

Meanwhile, cook the beef, sausage and onion in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and the meat reaches 160°F, 8 to 10 minutes. Spoon off extra fat. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato sauce, tomato paste, Italian seasoning, sugar, salt and pepper. Simmer 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
In a bowl, mix the ricotta, egg, 1/2 cup Parmesan and parsley.

Spread 1 cup of meat sauce in the baking dish. Layer 4 noodles, half the ricotta mixture, a third of the mozzarella and a third of the remaining sauce. Repeat once. Finish with the last 4 noodles, the rest of the sauce, the rest of the mozzarella and 1/4 cup Parmesan.
Cover with foil (tent it or spray the underside so it does not stick to the cheese). Bake 40 minutes. Uncover and bake 15 to 20 minutes more, until bubbling and the center reaches 165°F.
Let the lasagna rest 15 minutes before cutting so the layers hold together.
recipes.make_ahead: Assemble, cover tightly and refrigerate up to 1 day. Add about 15 minutes to the covered baking time, and check that the center reaches 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze assembled, unbaked lasagna wrapped well for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge 1 to 2 days, then bake as directed until 165°F in the center. Baked squares freeze well too.

leftovers.text: Squares reheat well for lunch; microwave covered until 165°F in the center.

recipes.kids: Children who are wary of ricotta often like it once it is baked in. Cut small squares for younger kids; it holds heat, so let it cool a few minutes.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free lasagna noodles (cook as the package says) and check the sausage label.
swaps.meatless: Replace the meat with 1 pound chopped mushrooms and 10 ounces thawed, squeezed frozen spinach, browned in a little olive oil.

prep_day.ahead: Make the meat sauce and assemble the whole lasagna; refrigerate or freeze unbaked.

recipes.name: Spaghetti with Meat Sauce
recipes.summary: A weeknight meat sauce that simmers while the pasta cooks. Double the sauce and freeze half.

ingredients.prep: for the pasta water (most is poured off, so it is left out of nutrition)

steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the beef, onion and carrot and cook, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and the beef reaches 160°F, about 8 minutes. Spoon off extra fat. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, Italian seasoning, sugar, salt, pepper and pepper flakes. Bring to a simmer, then lower the heat and cook 20 minutes, stirring now and then.
While the sauce simmers, bring a large pot of water to a boil with 1 tablespoon salt. Cook the spaghetti until tender, following the package time. Save 1/2 cup of the cooking water, then drain.
Toss the pasta with about half the sauce, adding a little pasta water if it looks dry. Serve the rest of the sauce on top with Parmesan.
recipes.make_ahead: The sauce keeps 3 to 4 days in the fridge. Reheat to 165°F and cook the pasta fresh.

freezer.text: Freeze the sauce (without pasta) for 2 to 3 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Leftover sauce makes quick sloppy joes or a topping for baked potatoes; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Serve some plain buttered noodles on the side with sauce for dipping. Break the spaghetti in half before cooking for easier eating.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free spaghetti.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the Parmesan.
swaps.meatless: Use 2 cups chopped mushrooms and 1 can drained lentils or white beans in place of the beef.

prep_day.ahead: Make a double batch of sauce; refrigerate one, freeze one.

recipes.name: Pot Roast with Carrots and Potatoes
recipes.summary: A Sunday-dinner classic you can make in the slow cooker or the oven. The leftovers make great sandwiches.
steps: Pat the roast dry and season all over with the salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large skillet (or the Dutch oven) over medium-high heat. Brown the roast well on all sides, about 10 minutes total. Browning adds flavor; you can skip it on a busy morning.

Slow cooker: Put the potatoes, carrots, celery and onion in the cooker and set the roast on top. Whisk the tomato paste into the broth with the Worcestershire and pour it over. Add the garlic, thyme and bay leaves. Cover and cook on low 8 to 9 hours or high 5 to 6 hours.
Oven: Heat the oven to 325°F. In the Dutch oven, add the onion, garlic, broth mixture, thyme and bay leaves around the roast. Cover and bake 2 1/2 hours. Add the vegetables and bake 1 hour more.
The roast is safe at 145°F, but chuck becomes fork-tender only after long cooking, when it pulls apart easily. Lift out the meat and vegetables and remove the bay leaves.

For gravy, pour the cooking liquid into a saucepan and bring to a boil. Stir the cornstarch into the water, whisk it in and simmer 1 to 2 minutes until thickened. Slice or pull the beef and serve with the vegetables and gravy.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

recipes.make_ahead: Cook a day ahead; chill the meat in its liquid. Lift off the hardened fat, then reheat gently to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze sliced beef in gravy for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Potatoes turn grainy when frozen, so eat those first.

leftovers.text: Pile leftover beef on rolls with a little gravy for hot sandwiches, or use it in beef stew or tacos; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Shred the beef and serve with the soft carrots. Let little ones dip pieces in the gravy.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free Worcestershire sauce and broth (check labels); cornstarch is gluten-free.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the vegetables and season the roast the night before; start the slow cooker in the morning.

recipes.name: Simple Roast Chicken
recipes.summary: A whole chicken roasted with lemon, garlic and herbs. Leftovers become soup, salads and quesadillas.
equipment: roasting pan or large oven-safe skillet
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Take the chicken out of its package and remove anything in the cavity. Do not rinse the chicken; washing raw poultry spreads germs around the sink. Pat it dry with paper towels and throw them away. Wash your hands and anything the raw chicken touched.
Lay the onion slices in the pan as a rack. Set the chicken on top, breast up.
Mix the butter, salt, pepper, thyme and garlic powder and rub it all over the chicken. Put the lemon halves and garlic cloves inside. Tie the legs together if you like.
Roast 1 hour 10 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes, until an instant-read thermometer reads 165°F in the thickest part of the breast and the innermost part of the thigh, without touching bone.
Let the chicken rest 15 minutes before carving. Spoon the pan juices over the meat.
Within 2 hours, pull the meat off the leftover carcass and refrigerate it. Save the bones in the freezer for stock if you like.
recipes.make_ahead: Rub the chicken with the seasoned butter up to 1 day ahead and keep it uncovered on a plate in the fridge; the skin dries and roasts crisper.

freezer.text: Freeze cooked, pulled chicken in portions for up to 4 months for best quality. Handy for soups, quesadillas and pot pie.

leftovers.text: Use leftover meat in chicken noodle soup, chicken quesadillas, Caesar salad or pot pie; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Many kids like the drumsticks. Pull the meat off the bone for younger children.

swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil instead of butter.

prep_day.ahead: Roast a chicken (or two) and pull the meat for the week.

recipes.name: Family Beef and Bean Chili
recipes.summary: Mild, hearty chili that feeds a crowd and freezes well. Let everyone add heat at the table.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the beef, onion and bell pepper and cook, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and the beef reaches 160°F, about 10 minutes. Spoon off extra fat.
Add the garlic, chili powder, cumin, oregano, paprika, salt and pepper. Cook 1 minute, stirring.
Stir in the crushed and diced tomatoes, beans, broth and brown sugar. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, partly cover and simmer 30 to 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.
Taste and add more salt or chili powder if you like. Serve with toppings.
Slow cooker: brown the beef and vegetables first (steps 1 and 2), then put everything in the cooker and cook on low 6 to 8 hours.
recipes.make_ahead: Chili tastes even better the next day. Refrigerate up to 4 days and reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Cool, then freeze in meal-size containers for 2 to 3 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Spoon over baked potatoes or hot dogs, or fill burritos; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Keep the pot mild and set out hot sauce for grown-ups. Kids like crushing a few tortilla chips on top.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the chili powder and broth labels.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the cheese and sour cream.
swaps.meatless: Skip the beef and add 2 more cans of beans plus 1 cup frozen corn.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the whole pot; portion some for lunches and freeze the rest.

recipes.name: Chicken and Vegetable Stir-Fry
recipes.summary: Tender chicken and crisp vegetables in a simple soy-ginger sauce. Have the rice cooking first.
steps: Whisk all the sauce ingredients together in a small bowl.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat. Add the chicken in one layer, sprinkle with the salt, and cook without stirring 2 minutes, then stir and cook until no longer pink inside and the pieces reach 165°F, about 4 minutes more. Move the chicken to a clean plate.
Add the remaining oil, the broccoli and carrot, and 2 tablespoons water. Cover and cook 2 minutes. Add the bell pepper and snap peas and stir-fry 2 minutes, until crisp-tender.
Return the chicken. Stir the sauce again (the cornstarch settles), pour it in and cook, stirring, until glossy and thick, about 1 minute.
Serve over rice (see Fluffy White Rice), topped with green onions and sesame seeds.
recipes.make_ahead: Cut the chicken and vegetables and mix the sauce up to 1 day ahead; keep raw chicken in its own covered container on the bottom shelf.

freezer.text: The vegetables go soft when frozen and reheated. Freeze raw cut chicken instead.

leftovers.text: Pack over rice for lunch; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Serve the sauce on the side for dipping, and let kids pick their vegetables.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari labeled gluten-free instead of soy sauce, and gluten-free broth.
swaps.meatless: Use 14 ounces firm tofu, pressed and cubed, browned in the oil.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the vegetables and chicken (separate containers); mix the sauce; cook the rice.

recipes.name: Sheet-Pan Sausage and Vegetables
recipes.summary: Smoked sausage roasted with potatoes, peppers and broccoli on one pan. Little to wash.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Line a large rimmed baking sheet with foil or parchment.
Toss the potatoes with 2 tablespoons oil and half the seasonings. Spread on the pan and roast 10 minutes.

Toss the sausage, pepper, onion and broccoli with the remaining oil and seasonings. Add to the pan, spread everything in one layer, and roast 15 minutes more, until the potatoes are tender and the sausage is browned and steaming hot (165°F).
recipes.make_ahead: Cut the vegetables and sausage up to 2 days ahead.

freezer.text: Roasted potatoes do not freeze well.

leftovers.text: Chop leftovers and scramble with eggs for breakfast; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Cut the sausage into half-moons for small children (round coins can be a choking risk).

swaps.gluten_free: Choose a sausage labeled gluten-free.
swaps.meatless: Use 2 cans drained chickpeas instead of sausage; add them with the vegetables.

prep_day.ahead: Chop everything and store the vegetables and sausage in one container.

recipes.name: Glazed Meatloaf
recipes.summary: Tender meatloaf with a sweet tomato glaze. Leftover slices make the best sandwiches.
equipment: 9-by-5-inch loaf pan or rimmed baking sheet
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. In a large bowl, stir the breadcrumbs into the milk and let them soak 5 minutes.
Add the eggs, 1/4 cup ketchup, Worcestershire, salt, pepper, Italian seasoning, onion and garlic and mix well. Add the beef and mix gently with your hands just until combined. Wash your hands.
Shape into a loaf about 9 by 5 inches on a lined baking sheet (it browns better than in a pan), or press into the loaf pan.
Stir the glaze ingredients together and spread half over the loaf.
Bake 45 minutes. Spread on the rest of the glaze and bake 10 to 20 minutes more, until a thermometer in the center reads 160°F.
Rest 10 minutes before slicing.
recipes.make_ahead: Shape the loaf, cover and refrigerate up to 1 day before baking; add about 10 minutes to the time.

freezer.text: Freeze baked slices separated with wax paper for 2 to 3 months, or the raw shaped loaf for 3 to 4 months, for best quality. Thaw in the fridge.

leftovers.text: Cold or warmed meatloaf on bread with ketchup is a lunchbox favorite; reheat to 165°F if serving warm.

recipes.kids: Bake some of the mixture in muffin tins (about 20 minutes, still to 160°F) for kid-size mini loaves.

swaps.gluten_free: Use 3/4 cup quick oats labeled gluten-free instead of breadcrumbs, and gluten-free Worcestershire.
swaps.dairy_free: Use water or unsweetened plant milk instead of milk.

prep_day.ahead: Mix and shape the meatloaf; refrigerate covered until baking night.

recipes.name: Cheesy Baked Ziti
recipes.summary: Pasta baked in marinara with ricotta and a blanket of mozzarella. Add browned meat if you like.

ingredients.prep: for the pasta water (most is poured off, so it is left out of nutrition)

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Cook the pasta in a large pot of boiling salted water for 2 minutes less than the package time. Drain.
If using sausage, brown it in a skillet, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F. Stir it into the sauce.
In a bowl, mix the ricotta, egg, half the Parmesan, Italian seasoning and pepper.

Toss the pasta with 1 1/2 jars of sauce. Spread half in the baking dish, dot with the ricotta mixture and sprinkle with half the mozzarella. Top with the rest of the pasta, the remaining sauce, mozzarella and Parmesan.
Cover with foil and bake 20 minutes. Uncover and bake 10 to 15 minutes more, until bubbling and 165°F in the center.
recipes.make_ahead: Assemble up to 1 day ahead, cover and refrigerate; add 10 to 15 minutes to the covered time and check for 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze unbaked in a foil pan, well wrapped, for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge and bake as directed.

leftovers.text: Reheat portions covered in the microwave to 165°F for lunches.

recipes.kids: Mix a portion without ricotta for picky eaters; it bakes the same.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free pasta and check the sauce label.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the ricotta and Parmesan, and use a dairy-free shredded cheese.

prep_day.ahead: Assemble the ziti and refrigerate or freeze it unbaked.

recipes.name: Chicken Noodle Soup
recipes.summary: A comforting pot of soup with tender chicken, carrots and egg noodles.
steps: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook 6 to 8 minutes, until softened. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add the broth, chicken, thyme, bay leaf, salt and pepper. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer 15 to 20 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F.
Lift out the chicken, shred it with two forks and return it to the pot. Remove the bay leaf.
Bring the soup back to a boil, add the noodles and cook until tender, 6 to 8 minutes. Stir in the parsley and taste for salt.
recipes.make_ahead: Make the soup base (without noodles) up to 4 days ahead. Reheat to a boil and cook the noodles in it just before serving, so they do not go mushy.

freezer.text: Freeze the soup without noodles for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Add fresh noodles when reheating.

leftovers.text: Pack hot soup in a preheated insulated food jar for school lunch: fill the jar with boiling water for a few minutes, empty it, then add soup heated to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Use small noodles or broken spaghetti for little spoons.

swaps.gluten_free: Use rice or gluten-free noodles and gluten-free broth.
swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil instead of butter.
swaps.meatless: Use vegetable broth and 2 cans drained white beans in place of the chicken.

prep_day.ahead: Make the soup base; cook noodles when serving.

recipes.name: Grilled Cheese and Tomato Soup
recipes.summary: A creamy tomato soup from pantry cans and golden grilled cheese for dipping.
steps: Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion 5 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, broth, sugar, basil, salt and pepper. Simmer 15 minutes.
Blend until smooth with an immersion blender (or carefully in a blender, filled no more than halfway with the lid vented). Stir in the half-and-half and warm through without boiling.
Butter one side of each bread slice. Put 4 slices butter side down in a skillet over medium-low heat, add 2 slices cheese each, and top with the other bread, butter side up.
Cook 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and the cheese melts. Cut and serve with the soup.
recipes.make_ahead: The soup keeps 4 days in the fridge; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze the soup before adding the half-and-half for 2 to 3 months for best quality; stir it in when reheating.

leftovers.text: Leftover soup makes a quick sauce for pasta.

recipes.kids: Cut sandwiches into strips for dipping.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free bread and broth.
swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil in the soup and skip the half-and-half (or use canned coconut milk); use dairy-free cheese and spread.

prep_day.ahead: Make the soup.

recipes.name: Breakfast-for-Dinner Sheet-Pan Hash
recipes.summary: Crispy potatoes, sausage and peppers on one pan, topped with eggs. Breakfast for dinner is a weeknight win.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the potatoes, bell pepper and onion with the oil, salt, paprika and pepper on a rimmed baking sheet. Roast 25 minutes, stirring once, until browned.
Meanwhile, brown the sausage in a skillet, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F. Drain on a paper towel.

Scatter the sausage over the potatoes. Make 8 small wells and crack an egg into each. Bake 8 to 10 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are firm. (USDA advises cooking eggs until the yolks and whites are firm.)
Sprinkle with cheese and green onions and serve.
recipes.make_ahead: Cube the potatoes and keep them covered in water in the fridge up to 1 day; drain and pat dry before roasting.

freezer.text: Best fresh.

leftovers.text: Wrap leftover hash and egg in a tortilla for a breakfast burrito; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Scramble the eggs separately for kids who do not like them baked.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the sausage label.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the cheese.
swaps.meatless: Skip the sausage and add 1 can drained black beans with the eggs.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the sausage; chop the peppers and onion.

recipes.name: Freezer Bean and Cheese Burritos
recipes.summary: A big batch of burritos to wrap and freeze for fast lunches and busy nights.
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onion 4 minutes. Stir in the refried beans, black beans, salsa, cumin, chili powder and salt and heat until steaming, 3 to 4 minutes. Let cool 10 minutes.
Warm the tortillas briefly so they fold without cracking.
Spread about 1/2 cup bean mixture and 1/4 cup rice down the center of each tortilla and top with 1/4 cup cheese. Fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
To eat now, toast seam side down in a skillet until golden. To freeze, wrap each burrito in foil or plastic and freeze in a bag.
From frozen: unwrap, wrap in a damp paper towel and microwave 2 to 3 minutes, turning halfway, until 165°F in the center. Or bake wrapped in foil at 375°F for 35 to 40 minutes.
recipes.make_ahead: The filling keeps 4 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze wrapped burritos for 2 to 3 months for best quality.

recipes.kids: Make a few smaller burritos in 8-inch tortillas for little appetites.

swaps.gluten_free: Use large corn or gluten-free tortillas (they crack more easily; warm them well).
swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free cheese or skip it and add diced avocado when serving.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the rice and filling, roll the burritos and freeze.

recipes.name: Chicken Quesadillas
recipes.summary: Crisp tortillas with melted cheese and chicken. A great way to use leftover roast or rotisserie chicken.
steps: Toss the chicken with the cumin, chili powder and salt.
Lay a tortilla flat and sprinkle half of it with 1/4 cup cheese, 1/2 cup chicken and another 1/4 cup cheese. Fold over. Repeat with the rest.
Brush a skillet lightly with oil and heat over medium. Cook quesadillas 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden and the cheese melts and the filling is hot (165°F for cooked chicken).
Cut into wedges and serve with salsa and sour cream.
recipes.make_ahead: Shred the chicken and mix the seasoning up to 3 days ahead (within 3 to 4 days of when the chicken was cooked).

freezer.text: Best fresh.

leftovers.text: Cold wedges are fine in a lunchbox with an ice pack.

recipes.kids: Cheese-only quesadillas are a good starting point; add a few beans or corn as they get adventurous.

swaps.gluten_free: Use corn tortillas (make smaller ones) and check the rotisserie chicken label.
swaps.meatless: Use 1 can drained black beans and 1 cup corn instead of chicken.

prep_day.ahead: Shred and season the chicken.

recipes.name: Vegetable Fried Rice
recipes.summary: Day-old rice, eggs and frozen vegetables become dinner in 20 minutes. Add leftover ham or chicken if you have it.

ingredients.prep: cooked a day ahead and chilled (makes about 4 cups)

steps: Heat 1 teaspoon oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the eggs and scramble until no liquid egg remains (egg dishes are done at 160°F). Move to a plate.
Add the rest of the oil and turn the heat to medium-high. Cook the onion 3 minutes, then the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the peas and carrots (and ham, if using) and cook 2 minutes.
Add the rice, breaking up clumps, and cook without stirring 1 minute so it crisps a little, then stir. Repeat a few times until the rice is hot, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the soy sauce, sesame oil, pepper, eggs and green onions.
recipes.make_ahead: Cook the rice a day ahead. Spread hot rice on a tray to cool quickly and refrigerate it within 2 hours.

freezer.text: Freeze cooled fried rice in portions for up to 1 month for best quality; reheat to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Pack for lunch and reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Kids can help crack and beat the eggs and stir in the peas.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari labeled gluten-free.
swaps.meatless: It is already meatless without the ham.

prep_day.ahead: Cook a big pot of rice for the week; cool quickly and refrigerate.

recipes.name: Lemon-Garlic Baked Salmon
recipes.summary: Salmon fillets baked with butter, lemon and garlic in about 15 minutes.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with foil or parchment and set the fillets skin side down on it.
Mix the melted butter, lemon juice and garlic and brush over the salmon. Sprinkle with salt, pepper and paprika.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 145°F and the flesh flakes easily with a fork.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
recipes.make_ahead: Mix the lemon-garlic butter up to 3 days ahead.

freezer.text: Freeze raw fillets instead; thaw overnight in the fridge before baking.

leftovers.text: Flake cold salmon onto a salad or into a wrap the next day.

recipes.kids: Check for pin bones by running a finger along the fillet before baking. A drizzle of honey on a kid portion helps (not for babies under 12 months).

swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil instead of butter.

prep_day.ahead: Thaw fillets in the fridge; mix the butter.

recipes.name: Skillet Pork Chops
recipes.summary: Golden, juicy boneless chops with a quick pan sauce.
steps: Pat the chops dry. Mix the salt, pepper, garlic powder and paprika and rub on both sides.
Heat the oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chops 4 to 5 minutes per side, until browned and a thermometer in the thickest part reads 145°F.
Move the chops to a clean plate and let them rest at least 3 minutes.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the broth, mustard and honey to the pan and scrape up the browned bits. Simmer 2 minutes, then swirl in the butter. Spoon over the chops.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

recipes.make_ahead: Season the chops up to 1 day ahead and refrigerate covered.

freezer.text: Freeze raw chops instead, 4 to 6 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Slice thin for sandwiches or fried rice; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Slice the chop into thin strips for younger children; 145°F pork can look slightly pink in the center and is safe after the rest.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free broth.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the butter in the sauce.

prep_day.ahead: Season the chops.

recipes.name: Shepherd's Pie
recipes.summary: Savory beef and vegetables under a mashed-potato crust. Made with beef it is often called cottage pie; use ground lamb for the classic.
steps: Cover the potatoes with cold salted water in a large pot, bring to a boil and cook 15 minutes, until very tender. Drain and mash with the butter, milk and salt.

Meanwhile, heat the oven to 400°F. Heat the oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the beef, onion and carrots, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and the beef reaches 160°F, about 8 minutes. Spoon off extra fat. Add the garlic for 1 minute.

Stir in the tomato paste and flour and cook 1 minute. Add the broth, Worcestershire, thyme, salt and pepper and simmer 5 minutes, until thick. Stir in the peas and corn. (Move to a baking dish if your skillet is not oven-safe.)
Spread the mashed potatoes over the filling to the edges and rough up the top with a fork. Sprinkle with cheese if you like.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until bubbling at the edges, golden on top and 165°F in the center.
recipes.make_ahead: Assemble, cool, cover and refrigerate up to 1 day. Bake about 15 minutes longer, until 165°F in the center.

freezer.text: Freeze assembled and unbaked, well wrapped, for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge before baking.

leftovers.text: Reheat portions covered to 165°F for lunch.

recipes.kids: Kids can help spread and swirl the potatoes.

swaps.gluten_free: Thicken with 1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons cold water instead of flour; check the Worcestershire and broth labels.
swaps.dairy_free: Mash the potatoes with olive oil and some of their cooking water; skip the cheese.
swaps.meatless: Use 2 cans drained lentils and 8 ounces chopped mushrooms instead of beef, with vegetable broth.

prep_day.ahead: Make the filling and mashed potatoes; assemble and refrigerate.

recipes.name: Hearty Beef Stew
recipes.summary: Chunks of beef simmered with potatoes and carrots until spoon-tender.
equipment: Dutch oven or large heavy pot (or slow cooker)
steps: Pat the beef dry, season with the salt and pepper, and toss with the flour.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the beef in two batches, 5 to 6 minutes per batch, adding the last of the oil as needed. Move to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the onion 4 minutes, then the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the broth, Worcestershire, thyme and bay leaves, scraping up the browned bits. Return the beef. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently 1 1/2 hours.

Add the potatoes, carrots and celery and simmer covered 30 to 40 minutes more, until the beef and vegetables are tender. (Beef is safe at 145°F; stew meat needs this long, gentle simmer to turn tender.) Stir in the peas for the last 5 minutes. Remove the bay leaves.
Slow cooker: after browning, put everything except the peas in the cooker and cook on low 8 hours. Stir in the peas at the end.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

recipes.make_ahead: Stew is even better the next day. Refrigerate up to 4 days; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Potatoes soften a little after freezing.

leftovers.text: Pack in a preheated insulated food jar for lunch; reheat to 165°F first.

recipes.kids: Cut the meat and vegetables a little smaller for young children.

swaps.gluten_free: Toss the beef in 2 tablespoons cornstarch instead of flour; check the broth and Worcestershire labels.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the stew start to finish; it reheats well all week.

recipes.name: Chicken Pot Pie
recipes.summary: Creamy chicken and vegetables under a flaky crust. Uses leftover or rotisserie chicken.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F with a baking sheet on the lower rack to catch drips.
Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion and celery 5 minutes. Stir in the flour and cook 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in the broth, then the milk. Simmer, stirring, until thick, about 3 minutes. Add the thyme, salt, pepper, chicken and peas and carrots.
Line the pie plate with one crust, pour in the filling and top with the second crust. Pinch the edges to seal, cut 4 small slits in the top and brush with the egg.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes, until the crust is deep golden and the filling bubbles and reaches 165°F. Let it rest 10 minutes before cutting.
recipes.make_ahead: Make the filling up to 2 days ahead and refrigerate. Assemble with cold filling and add 10 minutes to the baking time.

freezer.text: Freeze unbaked, well wrapped, for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Bake from frozen at 400°F for about 60 to 70 minutes (cover the edges with foil if they brown too fast) until 165°F in the center.

leftovers.text: Reheat wedges in the oven or microwave to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Kids can cut shapes from crust scraps to decorate the top.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free crust and thicken with 3 tablespoons cornstarch mixed into the cold milk.
swaps.meatless: Use 3 cups mixed vegetables and 1 can drained white beans instead of chicken, with vegetable broth.

prep_day.ahead: Make the filling; assemble on the night you bake.

recipes.name: Stovetop Mac and Cheese
recipes.summary: A smooth, creamy cheese sauce made in the same pot as the pasta.

ingredients.prep: for the pasta water (most is poured off, so it is left out of nutrition)

steps: Cook the macaroni in a large pot of boiling salted water until just tender. Drain and set aside.
In the same pot, melt the butter over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in the milk. Cook, whisking, until it thickens and coats a spoon, 4 to 5 minutes. Stir in the mustard, garlic powder and salt.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the cheese a handful at a time until smooth. Add the macaroni and stir to coat.
recipes.make_ahead: Best fresh. To reheat, add a splash of milk and warm gently, stirring, until hot (165°F).

freezer.text: Freeze portions for up to 2 months for best quality; the sauce may separate a little, so stir in milk while reheating.

leftovers.text: Spoon into a preheated insulated food jar for lunch.

recipes.kids: Stir in a cup of frozen peas or steamed broccoli with the pasta for extra vegetables.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free pasta and thicken with 2 tablespoons cornstarch whisked into the cold milk instead of flour.

prep_day.ahead: Shred the cheese.

recipes.name: Sloppy Joes
recipes.summary: Sweet and tangy saucy beef on soft buns, from pantry staples.
steps: Cook the beef, onion and pepper in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and the beef reaches 160°F, about 8 minutes. Spoon off extra fat. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato sauce, ketchup, brown sugar, Worcestershire, mustard, chili powder, salt and pepper. Simmer 10 minutes, until thick.
Spoon onto toasted buns.
recipes.make_ahead: The filling keeps 3 to 4 days in the fridge; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze the filling for 2 to 3 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Spoon leftover filling over baked potatoes or into a quesadilla.

recipes.kids: Serve open-faced with a fork for neater eating.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free buns and Worcestershire.
swaps.meatless: Use 2 cans drained lentils in place of the beef.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the filling.

recipes.name: Slow Cooker BBQ Pulled Pork
recipes.summary: Pork shoulder cooked low and slow, shredded and tossed with barbecue sauce. Feeds a crowd or a week of lunches.
steps: Mix the rub ingredients and rub all over the pork.
Lay the onion in the slow cooker, set the pork on top, and pour the broth and vinegar around it.
Cover and cook on low 8 to 10 hours (or high 5 to 6), until the pork pulls apart easily with a fork. It is safe at 145°F, but shoulder needs long cooking to become tender enough to shred.
Lift out the pork, shred it with two forks and discard any large pieces of fat. Skim the fat from the juices.
Return the meat to the cooker with 1 cup of the juices and the barbecue sauce. Stir and keep warm. Serve on buns with coleslaw.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

recipes.make_ahead: Cook up to 4 days ahead; reheat to 165°F with a splash of the juices.

freezer.text: Freeze shredded pork with some juices for 2 to 3 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Use in quesadillas, over baked potatoes, or on rice bowls; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Toss a portion with less sauce for kids who like it mild.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the barbecue sauce and broth labels; serve on gluten-free buns or over rice.

prep_day.ahead: Start the slow cooker in the morning; shred and portion in the evening.

recipes.name: Sheet-Pan Chicken Thighs and Potatoes
recipes.summary: Crispy-skinned chicken thighs roasted over potatoes and carrots on one pan.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Mix the salt, pepper, garlic powder, paprika and Italian seasoning.
Toss the potatoes and carrots with 2 tablespoons oil and half the seasoning and spread on the baking sheet.
Pat the chicken dry (do not rinse it), rub with the rest of the oil and seasoning, and set skin side up on the vegetables. Wash your hands.
Roast 35 to 45 minutes, until the skin is crisp and a thermometer in the thickest thigh, not touching bone, reads 165°F. Thighs stay juicy even if they go a bit higher.
recipes.make_ahead: Season the chicken up to 1 day ahead; cut the vegetables and keep the potatoes in water in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze raw thighs instead, up to 9 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Pull leftover meat for quesadillas or soup; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Take the skin off and cut the meat from the bone for young children.

prep_day.ahead: Season the chicken and cut the vegetables.

recipes.name: Sheet-Pan Chicken Fajitas
recipes.summary: Sliced chicken, peppers and onions roasted with a smoky spice mix and wrapped in warm tortillas.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Mix the chili powder, cumin, paprika, garlic powder and salt.
In a large bowl toss the chicken, peppers and onion with the oil and spices. Spread in one layer on the baking sheet (use two pans if crowded). Wash your hands and the bowl.
Roast 18 to 22 minutes, stirring once, until the vegetables are tender and the chicken is no longer pink inside and reaches 165°F.
Sprinkle with lime juice. Serve in warm tortillas with toppings.
recipes.make_ahead: Slice the vegetables and store them separately from the raw chicken up to 2 days ahead.

freezer.text: Freeze the raw chicken strips in the spice mix (in a bag) for up to 9 months for best quality; thaw in the fridge.

leftovers.text: Roll leftovers into a wrap or toss onto rice for lunch; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Let kids choose their own fillings; mild seasoning works for most.

swaps.gluten_free: Use corn tortillas.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the sour cream and cheese.
swaps.meatless: Use 2 cans drained black beans and 8 ounces sliced mushrooms instead of chicken.

prep_day.ahead: Slice the peppers and onions; mix the spices.

recipes.name: Lentil Vegetable Soup
recipes.summary: A thick, filling soup of lentils, carrots and tomatoes. Inexpensive and freezes well.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots and celery 6 to 8 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, cumin and thyme for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, tomatoes, broth, bay leaf, salt and pepper. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, partly cover and simmer 25 to 30 minutes, until the lentils are tender.
Remove the bay leaf. Stir in the spinach until wilted and add the lemon juice. Taste for salt.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 to 5 days in the fridge; it thickens, so add water when reheating to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze for 2 to 3 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Pack for lunch in a preheated insulated food jar.

recipes.kids: Blend part of the soup for a smoother texture, and serve with crackers or toast for dipping.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the broth label.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the soup.

recipes.name: Sheet-Pan Pizza Night
recipes.summary: One big pizza on a baking sheet, with half plain cheese and half toppings so everyone is happy.
steps: Let the thawed dough sit covered at room temperature 30 minutes so it stretches easily (or thaw in the fridge overnight, then do this).
Heat the oven to 450°F. Oil the baking sheet with 1 tablespoon oil. Press and stretch the dough to fill the pan; if it springs back, rest it 5 minutes and try again. Brush with the remaining oil.
Spread the sauce to within 1/2 inch of the edges and sprinkle with Italian seasoning, then mozzarella. Add toppings to half or all.
Bake on the lowest rack 15 to 20 minutes, until the crust is golden underneath and the cheese bubbles. Cool 5 minutes and cut into squares.
recipes.make_ahead: Shred the cheese and slice toppings the day before.

freezer.text: Freeze baked squares for 1 to 2 months for best quality; reheat at 400°F until hot.

leftovers.text: Cold pizza goes in lunchboxes with an ice pack, or reheat in a skillet.

recipes.kids: Give each child a corner to top themselves.

swaps.gluten_free: Use two gluten-free pizza crusts and bake as their package says.
swaps.meatless: Skip the pepperoni and add more vegetables.
swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free shredded cheese.

prep_day.ahead: Move the dough to the fridge to thaw; prep toppings.

recipes.name: Crispy Baked Fish Tacos
recipes.summary: Panko-coated white fish baked until crisp, with a quick lime slaw.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and oil the baking sheet.

Put the flour in one dish, beat the eggs in another, and mix the panko with chili powder, garlic powder and salt in the third. Pat the fish dry, coat in flour, dip in egg, and press into the panko. Set on the pan and drizzle with the oil. Wash your hands.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes, turning once, until golden and the fish flakes easily and reaches 145°F.
Meanwhile, toss the slaw ingredients together.
Fill warm tortillas with fish, slaw and toppings.
recipes.make_ahead: Mix the slaw dressing ahead; toss with the cabbage just before serving.

freezer.text: Best fresh.

leftovers.text: Reheat leftover fish in the oven to 165°F so it stays crisp.

recipes.kids: Serve the crispy fish as fish sticks with ketchup or tartar-style dip.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free panko and rice flour.
swaps.dairy_free: This recipe is dairy-free as written.

prep_day.ahead: Thaw fish in the fridge; mix the slaw dressing.

recipes.name: Turkey Taco Rice Bowls
recipes.summary: Seasoned ground turkey, rice, beans and corn in a bowl. Packs well for lunches.
steps: Cook the rice (see Fluffy White Rice).
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the turkey and onion, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and the turkey reaches 165°F, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the spices and salt for 1 minute, then the tomato sauce. Simmer 3 minutes.
Fill bowls with rice, turkey, beans, corn, tomatoes and cheese. Top with salsa and sour cream.
recipes.make_ahead: Pack the turkey, rice, beans and corn in containers for up to 4 days; add the cold toppings when serving.

freezer.text: Freeze the cooked turkey filling for 2 to 3 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Reheat the turkey, rice and beans to 165°F, then add the cold toppings.

recipes.kids: Serve the parts in separate piles on the plate.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the chili powder label.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the cheese and sour cream.
swaps.meatless: Use a second can of beans instead of turkey.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the rice and the turkey; pack bowls for lunches.

recipes.name: Fluffy Buttermilk Pancakes
recipes.summary: Tall, tender pancakes from scratch. Make extra and freeze them for school mornings.

ingredients.prep: melted, plus more for the pan

steps: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl whisk the buttermilk, eggs, melted butter and vanilla. Pour into the dry ingredients and stir just until no dry flour shows; small lumps are fine.

Heat a griddle or skillet over medium heat and brush with butter. Pour 1/4 cup batter per pancake. Cook until bubbles form on top and the edges look dry, 2 to 3 minutes. Flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more, until golden.
Keep cooked pancakes warm on a baking sheet in a 200°F oven while you finish the rest.
recipes.make_ahead: Mix the dry ingredients in a jar the night before.

freezer.text: Cool, freeze in one layer on a tray, then bag for up to 2 months for best quality. Reheat in the toaster or microwave.

leftovers.text: Spread a cold pancake with peanut butter and roll it up for a snack.

recipes.kids: Add blueberries or chocolate chips to the pancakes after pouring the batter. Kids can help whisk.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend with xanthan gum.
swaps.dairy_free: Use 1 3/4 cups unsweetened plant milk plus 2 tablespoons lemon juice for the buttermilk, and oil for the butter.

prep_day.ahead: Cook a double batch and freeze for weekdays.

recipes.name: Creamy Stovetop Oatmeal
recipes.summary: Old-fashioned oats cooked in milk and water with a little cinnamon. Set out toppings.
steps: Bring the water, milk and salt to a gentle boil in a saucepan over medium heat. Watch it; milk boils over quickly.
Stir in the oats and cinnamon. Lower the heat and simmer 5 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Take off the heat, cover and let stand 2 minutes. Serve with toppings.
recipes.make_ahead: Cook a big batch; refrigerate up to 4 days and reheat portions with a splash of milk.

freezer.text: Freeze cooked oatmeal in muffin-tin portions, then bag, for up to 2 months.

leftovers.text: Stir leftover oatmeal into pancake batter.

recipes.kids: Let kids choose two toppings. Cool the bowl a few minutes; oatmeal holds heat.

swaps.gluten_free: Use oats labeled gluten-free.
swaps.dairy_free: Use all water or an unsweetened plant milk.

prep_day.ahead: Cook a batch for the week.

recipes.name: Overnight Oats
recipes.summary: Oats soaked overnight in milk and yogurt. Grab-and-go breakfast with no cooking.
steps: Stir the oats, milk, yogurt, chia seeds, maple syrup, vanilla, cinnamon and salt together.
Divide among 4 jars, top with fruit, cover and refrigerate at least 8 hours or overnight.
Stir and eat cold, or microwave 1 to 2 minutes if you like it warm.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge; add delicate fruit like bananas the morning you eat it.

freezer.text: The texture suffers when frozen.

recipes.kids: Kids can layer their own jars the night before.

swaps.gluten_free: Use oats labeled gluten-free.
swaps.dairy_free: Use plant milk and a dairy-free yogurt.

prep_day.ahead: Fill jars for 4 days.

recipes.name: Soft Scrambled Eggs
recipes.summary: Tender, fluffy scrambled eggs in under 10 minutes.
steps: Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper until no streaks of white remain.
Melt the butter in a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Add the eggs and let them sit 20 seconds.

Push the eggs slowly from the edges to the center with a spatula, making large soft curds. Keep going until no liquid egg remains, 3 to 5 minutes (egg dishes are done at 160°F). Stir in cheese at the end if you like.
Serve right away with toast.
recipes.make_ahead: Best fresh.

freezer.text: Best fresh; use the breakfast burritos for a freezer egg breakfast.

recipes.kids: Kids old enough to use the stove with help can learn eggs first; they are quick and forgiving.

swaps.dairy_free: Use water instead of milk and olive oil instead of butter; skip the cheese.

recipes.name: Freezer Breakfast Burritos
recipes.summary: Eggs, sausage, potatoes and cheese wrapped and frozen for grab-and-go mornings.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the hash browns with the oil on a baking sheet and bake 20 minutes, until crisp.
Brown the sausage in a large skillet, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F. Drain on paper towels. Wipe out the skillet.
Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper. Scramble in the skillet over medium-low heat until no liquid egg remains. Let everything cool 10 minutes.
Divide the potatoes, sausage, eggs and cheese among the tortillas. Fold in the sides and roll tightly.
Wrap each in foil or plastic and freeze. To reheat: unwrap, wrap in a damp paper towel and microwave 1 1/2 to 2 1/2 minutes, turning once, until 165°F in the center.
recipes.make_ahead: Refrigerate wrapped burritos up to 3 days or freeze.

freezer.text: Freeze for 2 to 3 months for best quality.

recipes.kids: Make smaller burritos in 8-inch tortillas for little ones.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free tortillas and check the sausage label.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the milk and cheese.
swaps.meatless: Use 1 can drained black beans instead of sausage.

prep_day.ahead: Make and freeze the whole batch.

recipes.name: Veggie Egg Muffin Cups
recipes.summary: Mini baked omelets with vegetables and cheese. Reheat in seconds.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Coat a 12-cup muffin tin well with cooking spray (or use silicone liners).
Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper. Divide the spinach, pepper, green onions and cheese among the cups, then pour in the egg to about three-quarters full.
Bake 20 to 24 minutes, until puffed and set in the center (160°F).
Cool 5 minutes, then run a knife around each and lift out.
recipes.make_ahead: Refrigerate up to 4 days; microwave 30 to 45 seconds until hot (165°F).

freezer.text: Freeze in a bag for up to 2 months for best quality.

recipes.kids: Kids can choose their own fillings for a few cups; mark them with a toothpick.

swaps.dairy_free: Use water instead of milk and skip the cheese.
swaps.meatless: Already meatless; add diced ham for a meat version.

prep_day.ahead: Bake a batch for weekday breakfasts.

recipes.name: Cinnamon French Toast
recipes.summary: A good use for day-old bread: dipped in cinnamon custard and griddled until golden.

ingredients.prep: a day old if you have it

steps: Whisk the eggs, milk, sugar, vanilla, cinnamon and salt in a shallow dish.
Heat a griddle over medium heat and melt a little butter.
Dip each bread slice in the egg mixture for a few seconds per side, letting extra drip off. Cook 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden and no liquid egg remains in the center (160°F).
Serve with syrup and fruit.
recipes.make_ahead: Whisk the custard the night before and refrigerate.

freezer.text: Freeze cooked slices in one layer, then bag, for up to 2 months; reheat in the toaster.

recipes.kids: Cut into sticks for dipping in syrup.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free bread.
swaps.dairy_free: Use plant milk and oil.

prep_day.ahead: Make a batch and freeze.

recipes.name: Banana Oat Muffins
recipes.summary: Moist muffins that use up spotty bananas. Freeze and tuck into lunchboxes.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and line a muffin tin with paper liners.
Mash the bananas in a large bowl. Whisk in the oil, brown sugar, egg, yogurt and vanilla.
In another bowl, mix the flour, oats, baking soda, baking powder, cinnamon and salt. Add to the banana mixture and stir just until combined. Fold in chocolate chips if using.
Fill the cups about three-quarters full. Bake 18 to 22 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean.
Cool 5 minutes in the pan, then on a rack.
recipes.make_ahead: Keep at room temperature up to 2 days or in the fridge up to 5.

freezer.text: Freeze cooled muffins in a bag for up to 3 months. Pack frozen in a lunchbox; it thaws by lunchtime.

recipes.kids: Kids can mash the bananas and fill the liners.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend and oats labeled gluten-free.
swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free yogurt and dairy-free chips.

prep_day.ahead: Bake a batch; freeze half.

recipes.name: Yogurt Parfaits
recipes.summary: Layers of yogurt, fruit and granola. Kids can build their own.
steps: Spoon a layer of yogurt into each glass, then fruit, then a little granola. Repeat.
For lunchboxes, pack the granola separately so it stays crunchy, and include an ice pack.
recipes.make_ahead: Layer yogurt and fruit up to 1 day ahead; add granola when serving.

freezer.text: Best fresh.

recipes.kids: Set out bowls of toppings and let kids layer their own.

swaps.gluten_free: Use granola labeled gluten-free.
swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free yogurt.

prep_day.ahead: Wash and slice fruit; portion yogurt into jars.

recipes.name: Chicken Caesar-Style Salad
recipes.summary: Crisp romaine, Parmesan and croutons with an easy creamy dressing made without raw eggs.
steps: Pound the chicken to an even 3/4-inch thickness between sheets of plastic wrap. Rub with the oil and season with salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Cook in a skillet or grill pan over medium-high heat 5 to 6 minutes per side, until 165°F in the thickest part. Rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Whisk the dressing ingredients together. (Using mayonnaise instead of raw egg yolk keeps it safe to make ahead.)
Toss the romaine with about 2/3 of the dressing. Top with chicken, croutons and shaved Parmesan, and pass the rest of the dressing.
recipes.make_ahead: The dressing keeps 5 days in the fridge. Cook the chicken up to 3 days ahead.

freezer.text: Freeze cooked chicken only, not the salad.

leftovers.text: Pack dressing separately so the lettuce stays crisp.

recipes.kids: Serve the lettuce, chicken and croutons separately with dressing for dipping.

swaps.gluten_free: Skip the croutons and check the Worcestershire label.

prep_day.ahead: Cook and slice the chicken; make the dressing; wash and dry the romaine.

recipes.name: Turkey and Cheese Pinwheel Wraps
recipes.summary: Tortillas spread with cream cheese, rolled with turkey, cheese and spinach, and sliced into pinwheels.
steps: Spread each tortilla with cream cheese all the way to the edges (it holds the roll together).
Layer turkey, provolone and spinach over the bottom two-thirds. Lay a few cucumber strips near the bottom edge.
Roll up tightly from the bottom. Wrap in plastic and chill 15 minutes if you have time; they slice more neatly.
Cut into 1-inch pinwheels. Pack with an ice pack in an insulated lunch bag.
recipes.make_ahead: Rolled, wrapped wraps keep 1 day in the fridge; slice in the morning.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

recipes.kids: Pinwheels are easy for small hands. Swap in ham or cheese only.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free tortillas.
swaps.dairy_free: Use hummus instead of cream cheese and skip the provolone.
swaps.meatless: Use hummus, cheese and extra vegetables.

prep_day.ahead: Roll the wraps the night before.

recipes.name: Lunchbox PB and J (Nut-Free Option)
recipes.summary: The classic, with a sunflower seed butter swap for schools that do not allow nuts.
steps: Spread 4 slices of bread with peanut butter (or sunflower seed butter) all the way to the edges; this keeps the jam from soaking in.
Spread jam on the other 4 slices, add banana if you like, and close the sandwiches.
Cut and pack. Make sandwiches the night before if mornings are rushed.
recipes.make_ahead: Make up to 1 day ahead; keep refrigerated.

freezer.text: Peanut butter and jam sandwiches (without banana) freeze for up to 1 month; pack frozen and they thaw by lunch.

recipes.kids: Use a cookie cutter for fun shapes. Check your school rules on nuts before packing peanut butter.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free bread.

prep_day.ahead: Make and freeze a week of sandwiches.

recipes.name: Classic Tuna Salad Sandwiches
recipes.summary: Canned tuna with a little crunch from celery and pickle relish.
steps: Flake the tuna in a bowl. Stir in the mayonnaise, celery, relish, lemon juice and pepper.
Spread on bread with lettuce. Pack with an ice pack.
recipes.make_ahead: Tuna salad keeps 3 to 5 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Mayonnaise-based salads do not freeze well.

recipes.kids: Serve on crackers or in a wrap. Light tuna is lower in mercury than albacore, and the FDA lists it among its best choices for children.

swaps.gluten_free: Serve in lettuce cups or on gluten-free bread.

prep_day.ahead: Mix the tuna salad.

recipes.name: Italian Pasta Salad
recipes.summary: Rotini with vegetables, mozzarella and Italian dressing. Better after a night in the fridge.

ingredients.prep: for the pasta water (most is poured off, so it is left out of nutrition)

steps: Cook the pasta in boiling salted water until just tender. Drain and rinse with cold water to cool; drain well.
Toss with the vegetables, olives, mozzarella and dressing. Add pepperoni and Parmesan if you like.
Chill at least 1 hour. Stir in a splash more dressing before serving if it looks dry.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 3 to 5 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Does not freeze well.

leftovers.text: Pack with an ice pack for lunches.

recipes.kids: Leave the olives on the side for kids who are unsure.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free pasta.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the cheeses and add a can of drained chickpeas.

prep_day.ahead: Make the whole salad for lunches.

recipes.name: Hummus Veggie Wraps
recipes.summary: Hummus, crunchy vegetables and feta rolled in a tortilla.
steps: Spread each tortilla with 1/4 cup hummus.
Layer the vegetables and feta along the bottom third, roll up tightly and cut in half.
Pack with an ice pack.
recipes.make_ahead: Best the day you make it; vegetables can be cut up to 3 days ahead.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

recipes.kids: Offer the vegetables as dippers with hummus instead of a wrap.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free tortillas.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the feta.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the vegetables.

recipes.name: Fluffy White Rice
recipes.summary: Simple stovetop long-grain rice. Cook extra for fried rice and burritos.
equipment: medium saucepan with a tight lid
steps: Rinse the rice in a strainer until the water runs mostly clear. This keeps it from getting gummy.
Bring the water, salt and butter to a boil in a saucepan. Stir in the rice, cover, and turn the heat to low.
Cook 15 to 18 minutes, until the water is absorbed. Take off the heat and let stand covered 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
To keep leftovers safely, spread the rice out to cool and refrigerate it within 2 hours.
recipes.make_ahead: Refrigerate cooked rice up to 4 days; reheat to 165°F with a splash of water.

freezer.text: Freeze cooled rice flat in bags for up to 3 months.

leftovers.text: Use cold rice for fried rice.

recipes.kids: Stir in frozen peas for the last 5 minutes for color.

swaps.dairy_free: Use oil or skip the butter.

prep_day.ahead: Cook a double batch for the week.

recipes.name: Baked Brown Rice
recipes.summary: Hands-off brown rice baked in the oven, which cooks it evenly every time.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Spread the rice in the baking dish.
Bring the water, butter and salt to a boil (kettle or microwave) and pour over the rice. Cover tightly with foil.
Bake 1 hour. Uncover, fluff with a fork and let stand 5 minutes.
recipes.make_ahead: Refrigerate up to 4 days; cool quickly and refrigerate within 2 hours.

freezer.text: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months.

leftovers.text: Add to soups or burrito bowls.

recipes.kids: Mix half brown and half white rice to start.

swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil instead of butter.

prep_day.ahead: Bake a batch while something else roasts.

recipes.name: Roasted Vegetables
recipes.summary: Broccoli, carrots and peppers roasted until browned at the edges. Works with almost any vegetable.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss everything on a large baking sheet and spread in one layer; crowding makes them steam instead of brown.
Roast 20 to 25 minutes, stirring once, until tender and browned at the edges.
recipes.make_ahead: Cut the vegetables up to 3 days ahead.

freezer.text: Roasted vegetables turn soft when frozen.

leftovers.text: Add to pasta, quesadillas or egg muffin cups.

recipes.kids: A sprinkle of Parmesan in the last 5 minutes wins over many kids.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the vegetables.

recipes.name: Simple Green Salad
recipes.summary: Crisp greens and vegetables with a shake-in-a-jar vinaigrette.
steps: Shake the vinaigrette ingredients in a jar until blended.
Toss the greens and vegetables with dressing just before serving.
recipes.make_ahead: The vinaigrette keeps 1 week in the fridge; shake before using. Wash and dry greens up to 3 days ahead and store with a paper towel.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

recipes.kids: Serve dressing on the side for dipping.

prep_day.ahead: Wash greens; make the vinaigrette.

recipes.name: Creamy Mashed Potatoes
recipes.summary: Buttery, smooth mashed potatoes made with yellow potatoes.

ingredients.prep: for the cooking water (left out of nutrition)

steps: Put the potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold water by 1 inch and add 1 tablespoon salt. Bring to a boil and cook 15 to 20 minutes, until a fork slides in easily.
Drain well and return to the pot over low heat for 1 minute to dry.
Mash with the butter, then stir in the warm milk, salt and pepper.
recipes.make_ahead: Make up to 2 days ahead; reheat covered in the oven or microwave to 165°F with a splash of milk.

freezer.text: Freeze in portions for up to 1 month; they may be a little looser after thawing.

leftovers.text: Top shepherd's pie or make potato pancakes.

recipes.kids: Kids can do the mashing once the potatoes cool a little.

swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil and some of the potato cooking water or unsweetened plant milk.

prep_day.ahead: Make and refrigerate.

recipes.name: Garlic Butter Green Beans
recipes.summary: Bright green beans steamed and tossed with garlic butter.
steps: Put the beans and water in a large skillet, cover and cook over medium-high heat 5 to 6 minutes, until crisp-tender.
Uncover and let any water boil off. Add the butter, garlic and salt and toss 1 minute. Squeeze in the lemon juice.
recipes.make_ahead: Trim the beans up to 3 days ahead.

freezer.text: Use frozen green beans instead if you like; cook them a little less.

recipes.kids: Call them "green fries" and let kids eat them with their fingers.

swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil.

prep_day.ahead: Trim the beans.

recipes.name: Buttered Corn on the Cob
recipes.summary: Sweet summer corn boiled or grilled and brushed with butter.
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add the corn and cook 4 to 6 minutes, until tender.
Or grill over medium-high heat 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until lightly charred.
Brush with butter and sprinkle with salt.
recipes.make_ahead: Best fresh. In winter, use 4 cups frozen corn heated with the butter.

freezer.text: Best fresh.

leftovers.text: Cut the kernels off leftover ears for salads, quesadillas or chili.

recipes.kids: Break ears in half for small hands. For young children, cut the kernels off the cob.

swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil.

recipes.name: Garlic Bread
recipes.summary: Crusty bread spread with garlic butter and baked until golden.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Split the loaf lengthwise.
Mix the butter, garlic, parsley and salt; spread on the cut sides. Sprinkle with Parmesan if you like.
Bake cut side up 10 to 12 minutes, until golden at the edges. Slice.
recipes.make_ahead: Spread the bread, wrap in foil and refrigerate up to 1 day.

freezer.text: Freeze the buttered, unbaked bread wrapped in foil for up to 2 months; bake from frozen about 15 minutes.

recipes.kids: Toast a few slices without garlic for very young eaters.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free bread.
swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil instead of butter.

prep_day.ahead: Butter the loaf and freeze.

recipes.name: Crispy Roasted Potatoes
recipes.summary: Golden potato chunks with crisp edges and soft centers.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F with the baking sheet inside.
Toss the potatoes with the oil and seasonings. Carefully spread them on the hot pan in one layer.
Roast 30 to 35 minutes, turning once, until crisp and browned.
recipes.make_ahead: Cut the potatoes and keep covered in water in the fridge up to 1 day; dry well before roasting.

freezer.text: Best fresh.

leftovers.text: Chop into a breakfast hash.

recipes.kids: Serve with ketchup for dipping.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the potatoes.

recipes.name: Creamy Coleslaw
recipes.summary: Crunchy cabbage slaw with a tangy-sweet dressing; great on pulled pork sandwiches.
steps: Whisk the mayonnaise, vinegar, sugar, celery seed, salt and pepper.
Toss with the coleslaw mix and chill at least 30 minutes.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; it softens over time.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

recipes.kids: Some kids like it best with a handful of raisins or apple matchsticks.

prep_day.ahead: Make the slaw.

recipes.name: Cornbread Muffins
recipes.summary: Lightly sweet cornbread baked as muffins. Perfect with chili and soups.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Grease a 12-cup muffin tin or line it with paper.
Whisk the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder and salt. In another bowl whisk the milk, egg and oil.
Stir the wet ingredients into the dry just until combined. Divide among the cups.
Bake 14 to 17 minutes, until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.
recipes.make_ahead: Keep 2 days at room temperature.

freezer.text: Freeze for up to 3 months.

recipes.kids: Serve with honey butter (not for babies under 12 months).

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend.
swaps.dairy_free: Use unsweetened plant milk.

prep_day.ahead: Bake and freeze.

recipes.name: Rainbow Fruit Salad
recipes.summary: A colorful bowl of fresh fruit with a squeeze of orange.
steps: Rinse the fruit under running water before cutting.
Combine everything in a bowl and toss gently with the lemon juice, which keeps the banana from browning.
recipes.make_ahead: Cut fruit (except banana) keeps 2 to 3 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Do not freeze (use leftover fruit in smoothies).

leftovers.text: Spoon over yogurt or oatmeal.

recipes.kids: Cut grapes lengthwise into quarters for children under 4; whole grapes are a choking risk.

prep_day.ahead: Wash and cut fruit.

recipes.name: No-Bake Oat Energy Bites
recipes.summary: Oats, peanut butter and a few chocolate chips rolled into bite-size balls.
steps: Stir everything together in a bowl until evenly mixed. If too sticky, chill 15 minutes.
Roll into 24 balls about 1 inch across and set on wax paper.
Chill at least 30 minutes to firm up.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 1 week in the fridge in a covered container.

freezer.text: Freeze up to 3 months.

recipes.kids: Kids love to roll these. Contains honey, so not for babies under 12 months.

swaps.gluten_free: Use oats labeled gluten-free.
swaps.dairy_free: Use dairy-free chocolate chips.

prep_day.ahead: Roll a batch for the week.
